metaTitle: Best 28 Inch Griddles for Family Cooks, 2026
metaDescription: Five 28 inch Blackstone griddles compared on zone count, hood, measured square inches and bundle contents, so you pick the right family size model.
expertTake: The Blackstone 2403 28 inch XL with three heat zones is the best pick because it adds a third zone to the family size plate. The 1517 is the value pick if you accept no hood. Skip a 28 inch griddle if you routinely cook for ten or more, because a plate this size runs out of room before the party does. Whichever you choose, pair it with a soft cover and a flat scraper from the first day.
introParagraphs: The 28 inch griddle is the size most households end up owning. It is wide enough to cook breakfast for a family and small enough for a normal patio, which is why every maker offers one and why the variations between them are subtle.
Those variations come down to how many zones the plate has, whether a hood comes with it and what ships in the box. Reading them correctly turns an apparent coin flip into a clear decision.

products.name: Blackstone 2403 28 Inch XL Omnivore Griddle with Hood, 3 Zones
products.description:
The 2403 is the 28 inch Blackstone with three independently controlled zones, which is the feature that matters most at this size. With three zones you can sear at one end, cook at medium in the centre and hold food warm at the other end, rather than treating the plate as one big hotplate.

The listing calls this the XL, which suggests a plate with more room than the standard 28 inch models, though you should compare any stated area rather than trusting the name alone. The Omnivore plate carries the wind guards and faster preheat typical of the brand, and the hood keeps the surface clean between uses.

Against the two burner 2367 that shares the 28 inch label, the 2403 costs more but gives you the extra zone and the extra cooking flexibility. If you cook full meals instead of just breakfast, that third zone is worth paying for. The usual routine of scraping hot, oiling and covering applies, and the hood adds some protection but is no replacement for a soft cover in wet seasons. Setup is the part owners underestimate, because a three burner cart with a hood and shelves takes a patient hour with the instructions and a helper for the heavier lifts. Once it is together, keep an eye on the knob and igniter connections after the first few uses, since new hardware settles in. It is also the model to choose if you plan to keep the griddle for many years, since the zone control is the feature people grow into rather than out of.
products.bestFor: Families who cook full meals and want three zones on a manageable plate.
pros: Three independently controlled heat zones
Omnivore plate with wind guards
Hood protects the plate between cooks
Extra plate room in the XL layout
cons: Costs more than the two burner models
Bare steel still needs oiling and covering

products.name: Blackstone 1883 28 Inch Omnivore Griddle with Hood and Shelves
products.description:
The 1883 is the long-running family griddle: a 28 inch plate, a hood and counter height side shelves on a powder coated cart. It is the safe pick because the layout is well known and parts are easy to match.

The counter height shelves are a quiet advantage. They give you a surface at the same level as the plate for tools, plates and seasonings, which makes real cooking less awkward than on a tabletop machine.

Compared with the 2403 it has fewer zones, so you manage heat by moving food rather than by adjusting a third burner. Compared with the 1517 it adds the hood. For most people who just want a good griddle without fuss, it is the sensible middle. Maintenance is the standard flat top routine, plus a soft cover through the wet season. A practical note is that the powder coated frame is tougher than bare steel but not immune to chips, so touch up scrapes with high heat paint before moisture finds the metal underneath. Expect to wheel it to a sheltered spot in storms, because the hood is a defence against drizzle, not against driving rain. If you are choosing between this and the 1517, the hood and shelves are the whole difference worth paying for.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a proven layout with a hood and useful shelves.
pros: Hood and shelves in one package
Counter height shelving for tools
Wind guards on the Omnivore plate
Well-established design with easy-to-match parts
cons: Powder coat chips if knocked, exposing steel

products.name: Blackstone 2450AZ 28 Inch Griddle Bundle with Soft Cover and Spatulas
products.description:
The 2450AZ is the 28 inch hooded griddle sold with a compatible soft cover and two spatulas. It exists to answer the question new owners ask on day one: what else do I need to buy?

The cover is the important item, because rain and dew are the main enemies of a seasoned steel plate. The spatulas get you through the first few cooks, after which most owners buy a heavier pair and a scraper.

The griddle hardware is in the same family as the 1883, so you are paying for the extras, not for a different cooking machine. If you would have bought a cover anyway, the bundle can be the tidy option. If you already own tools and a cover, the plain 1883 or 2403 is the better use of money. Always confirm the cover fits your model before you rely on it. Treat the bundle as a convenience purchase with a clear break-even: if the cover and tools would cost you a similar amount separately, you are paying for the box and nothing more. It also shortens the awkward first week, when new owners cook on an uncovered plate because the cover has not arrived yet. Keep the packaging notes, since the cover size is the detail owners most often get wrong when reordering.
products.bestFor: First time owners who want everything in one order.
pros: Soft cover included from day one
Two spatulas supplied
Hood and plate in the family design
Saves a second shopping trip

products.name: Blackstone 2367 28 Inch Omnivore Griddle with Hood, 2 Burners
products.description:
The 2367 is a two burner 28 inch griddle with two independently controlled cooking zones. The listing describes it as portable and includes seasoning, which is the first thing a bare plate needs.

Two zones are enough for a hot side and a cool side, but not enough for three-stage cooking. It makes sense when your cooks are typically one main and one side, or when you value a simpler build with fewer burners to maintain.

A two burner layout also uses less propane than the three or four burner units, which matters on a camping or tailgate trip where fuel is limited. The hood protects the plate in transit. Compared with the 2403 it gives up a zone for a lower price tier, and compared with the 1517 it adds a hood. Look at it as the compact, efficient option within the 28 inch family. Because it has only two burners, recovery after a cold load is slower than on the three zone 2403, so cook in smaller batches rather than dumping a whole tray of frozen patties at once. Portability is the real selling point: with fewer burners, less weight and a hood, it rides in a trunk more happily than the heavier carts. Keep the seasoning that comes with it handy for the first oiling passes.
products.bestFor: Smaller households and portable cooks who want two zones and a hood.
pros: Two independent zones for hot and cool sides
Hood protects the plate
Seasoning included in the listing
Lower fuel use than larger burner counts
cons: Less flexible than the three zone 2403

products.name: Blackstone 1517 28 Inch Omnivore Griddle, 517 sq in
products.description:
The 1517 is the 28 inch griddle with the fewest frills. The listing gives 517 square inches of plate and a rear grease management system, and the Omnivore plate brings the same wind guards and fast preheat as the pricier models.

With grease leaving through the rear, the front of the griddle stays free for you. That is a small design choice that makes the machine nicer to work at over the years.

Without a hood, the plate is exposed. A cover is not optional and oiling after each cook is more important, because rust is the most common reason an outdoor griddle gets replaced. Against the hooded 1883 it costs less and weighs less. If you want 28 inches of cooking for the smallest outlay and you will be disciplined about covers, this is the pick. Owners who choose it tend to be tinkerers who already own a cover and a scraper and like a machine with nothing extra to break. The rear grease path is the feature to notice in practice, because it keeps drips away from your forearms and from the front shelf.
products.bestFor: Disciplined owners who want the lowest cost 28 inch plate.
pros: 517 square inches listed on the plate
Rear grease keeps the front clear
Omnivore plate with wind guards
Lowest cost in the 28 inch group
cons: No hood leaves the plate exposed
Needs a cover and routine oiling

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 28 inch plate with three zones like the 2403 lets you sear, cook and hold at once, while the two burner 2367 gives only a hot side and a cool side. The 1883 and 1517 sit between in capability depending on their burner layout. Decide how many dishes you cook at different temperatures, and pay for the zones you will actually use. If you routinely cook at three temperatures, the third burner is the single upgrade that changes how a meal comes together.

A 28 inch class plate lands around 500 to 520 square inches, and the 1517 states 517. That is enough for about eight to ten burgers in a pass. If a listing gives no area figure, treat the width as a rough guide only. A mid-size plate also loses less heat to the edges than a large one, so the figure is more usable than it looks.

A hood protects seasoning and lets you melt and steam, while an open plate is cheaper and lower. The 2403, 1883, 2450AZ and 2367 include one, the 1517 does not. Outdoors all year, take the hood. Hoods also reduce the amount of fine ash and leaf litter that lands in a plate left uncovered for a weekend.

The 2450AZ ships with a soft cover and two spatulas and the 2367 lists seasoning. Compare the contents rather than the headline, because the cooking hardware is largely the same family. A bundle saves a trip but not much else. Whether you want the cover and tools is a personal question, but they are the first two things most new owners lack.

The 1517 sends grease out the back, which keeps the front clear. Any flat top needs a drain that does not clog. Check the cup position before you buy. A long reach to empty the drain is the sort of annoyance that only shows up after a month of use.

Even hooded models need a soft cover in wet weather, because the hood does not seal. A bundle that includes one, like the 2450AZ, fixes the first wet month. Plan your storage before you buy. Even a good cover is only effective if it is dry when you put it on, so wipe down condensation first.

howWeEvaluated.title: Zones and plate
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared zone count and stated plate area across the five models. The 2403's three zones and the 1517's 517 square inches were the clearest numbers. Zones counted for more than raw size.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weather readiness
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked for hoods and the cover options in the listing. Hooded models scored better, and the bundle's cover earned credit. The 1517 lost points for exposure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cost of ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered seasoning effort, covers and parts matching. Established layouts like the 1883 are easy to maintain. Bare steel always carries rust risk.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability and fuel use
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted the two burner 2367's lower fuel use and portable positioning. Fixed carts scored on stability. Fuel use matters most for travelling cooks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We read listings for repeat themes such as chipped powder coat and wobbly shelves. Those informed the cons and the ranking, not any numeric score.

cards.label: Two zones
cards.text: The 2367 gives a hot side and a cool side and burns less propane. It suits simple cooks and portable use.

cards.label: Three zones
cards.text: The 2403 lets you sear, cook and hold at the same time. It suits full meals and entertaining.

howToChoose.note: If you cook a main and a side, take the 2367. If you cook three things at once, take the 2403.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Seasoning, a cover and basic tools in the first order, since a bare plate cannot be used safely out of the box without them. Simplicity helps.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The 2450AZ includes a cover and spatulas, the 2367 lists seasoning. Both ease the first month.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You host or cook varied menus, so the three zone 2403 earns its place.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cook simple meals for two to four. The 1517 or 2367 gives you the plate without the extras.

maintenance.why: Warm residue lifts in one pass. Cold residue sticks and burns on later. It prevents the stuck-on layer that takes a scraper and elbow grease to remove.
The film keeps moisture off bare steel. It is the rust defence that costs almost nothing. Pick a high smoke point oil and wipe nearly all of it off so it does not turn tacky.
A full cup spills on the cart or patio. Check it before lighting. It is a ten second job that prevents a messy surprise.
The hood does not seal. A soft cover keeps rain and debris off. Wipe off condensation before fitting the cover to avoid trapping damp.
Soapy water shows leaks as bubbles. Replace any leaking part before use. Do it with the cylinder disconnected from any ignition source.

faq.q: Is 28 inches big enough for a family?
faq.a: Yes for most families. A 28 inch class plate is around 500 to 520 square inches, enough for roughly eight to ten burgers in one pass. Anything wider mostly adds steel to heat rather than a better cooking experience for a small household.

Only if you cook several dishes at different temperatures. For one main and one side, two zones are plenty and use less propane. The extra burner also adds one more valve and igniter to look after over the years.
If the griddle lives outdoors, yes. It protects seasoning and enables melting, though a soft cover still belongs on top.

faq.q: What does XL mean on the 2403?
faq.a: It is a model designation, not a measurement. Compare the stated plate area rather than relying on the name. The brand lists the zones and the hood, which matter more than the label.
Only if you need the cover and tools. The cooking hardware in the 2450AZ matches the family design.

faq.q: Can it be used on a balcony?
faq.a: Rules depend on fire code, your lease and the manufacturer. Propane is the most restricted fuel in many buildings, so check first.
